title: 绝句·两个黄鹂
pinyin: Jué Jù · Liǎng Gè Huáng Lí
author: Du Fu

translation: two orioles sing in the emerald willows
a row of white egrets climbs into the blue sky
my window frames the thousand-year snow of the western ridge
boats that sailed ten thousand miles from eastern wu lie at my door

appreciation: Two orioles, a line of egrets, distant snow, and ships from far away are packed into four lines like a painted scroll. Yellow against green, white against blue, and a window frame that turns a vast landscape into something intimate. The poem matters because Du Fu builds a whole bright world from color and scale here, proving that his eye for joy was as sharp as his eye for grief.
